ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The single square tile in the attached figure is divided by several diagonals into triangular regions; the triangular region corresponding to the bottom side is white, and the other regions touching the upper side, left side, and right side are dark/black. Therefore, looking at the boundary colors, this kind of tile has exactly 1 white side and 3 black sides; rotating the tile is equivalent to choosing which direction this 1 white side faces. Reasoning: Represent each tile placed in the 5×5 grid by “the direction faced by its unique white side.” The common side of two adjacent tiles must have the same color, so there are only two legal cases: both tiles face their white sides toward this common side, and the common side is white; or neither tile faces toward this common side, and the common side is black. Let p be the number of white unit sides on the outer boundary, and q be the number of internal white common sides. Each tile contributes exactly 1 white side, for a total contribution of 25 white sides. An outer-boundary white side consumes the white side of 1 tile, and an internal white common side is contributed by 1 white side from each of the two adjacent tiles, so p + 2q = 25. To make the number of black sides on the outer boundary as small as possible, the number p of white sides on the outer boundary must be made as large as possible, that is, q must be made as small as possible. The 5×5 grid has 3×3=9 internal cells. These internal tiles have no side on the outer boundary of the large square, so their white sides must point toward adjacent tiles, and must be matched in pairs as internal white common sides. Since 9 is an odd number, the 9 internal tiles cannot be completely paired only among themselves internally; at least 1 boundary tile must also be paired with some internal tile. Therefore at least 10 tiles have their white sides used for internal pairing, that is, q ≥ 5. From p + 2q = 25, we get p ≤ 25 - 10 = 15. The outer boundary of the large square has altogether 20 unit sides, so the number of black sides on the outer boundary is at least 20 - 15 = 5. This lower bound can be attained: use row and column coordinates to mark the 5×5 grid, and let the internal white pairings be (1,2)-(2,2), (2,3)-(2,4), (3,2)-(4,2), (3,3)-(4,3), (3,4)-(4,4). These 5 pairs cover 9 internal cells and 1 boundary cell. The remaining 15 boundary tiles all place their white sides facing outward. In this way the outer boundary has 15 white unit sides, so the black unit sides are 20 - 15 = 5.

method.method_draft: Read the tile image as a square tile whose boundary has exactly one white side and three black sides; rotations of this same pattern are what allow adjacent unit tiles to match colors. Model each placed tile by the direction of its single white side. A shared edge is valid only if either both neighboring tiles point their white side at each other, or neither does. Let p be the number of white perimeter segments and q the number of internal white shared edges. Since there are 25 tiles and each contributes exactly one white side, p + 2q = 25. To maximize p, minimize q. The 9 interior cells cannot put their white side on the outer perimeter, so their white sides must be used in internal matched pairs. Since 9 is odd, at least one boundary tile must also be involved in such a pair, so at least 10 tile white-sides are internal, meaning q >= 5 and p <= 15. Therefore the perimeter has at least 20 - 15 = 5 black segments. Show attainability by pairing the 9 interior tiles plus one adjacent boundary tile into 5 internal white pairs, and orienting all other boundary tiles outward, giving 15 white perimeter segments and hence 5 black segments.

由 p + 2q = 25 得 p ≤ 25 - 10 = 15。大正方形外周共有 20 条单位边，所以外周黑色边数至少为 20 - 15 = 5。

这个下界可以达到：用行列坐标标记 5×5 方格，令内部白色配对为 (1,2)-(2,2)、(2,3)-(2,4)、(3,2)-(4,2)、(3,3)-(4,3)、(3,4)-(4,4)。这 5 对覆盖了 9 个内部格子和 1 个边界格子。其余 15 个边界瓷砖都把白色边朝外放置。这样外周有 15 条白色单位边，故黑色单位边为 20 - 15 = 5。

method.method_draft: Read the image as giving a one-white-side tile, so each tile orientation can create at most one white perimeter edge. First ask whether fewer than 5 black perimeter segments is possible. The perimeter has 20 unit segments, so fewer than 5 black would mean at least 16 white perimeter segments. But there are exactly 16 boundary tiles in a 5 by 5 grid, and each boundary tile has only one white side, so this would force every boundary tile to place its white side outward on the perimeter. Then no boundary tile could use its white side to match an interior tile. The 9 non-boundary tiles would have to match their white sides only among themselves in adjacent pairs, which is impossible because 9 is odd. Hence at least 5 black perimeter segments are necessary. For sufficiency, pair eight of the nine interior tiles into four adjacent white-white pairs, pair the remaining interior tile with one neighboring boundary tile, and orient every other boundary tile with its white edge outward. This leaves exactly one boundary tile not contributing a white perimeter edge; since corner tiles can only contribute one white perimeter edge anyway, the total white perimeter can be 15, so the black perimeter count is 20 - 15 = 5.

因此最小可能的黑色周长边数是 5。

raw_record.original_question: A $5 \times 5$ square is made from $1 \times 1$ tiles, all with the same pattern, as shown. Any two adjacent tiles have the same colour along the shared edge. The perimeter of the $5 \times 5$ square consists of black and white segments of length 1. What is the smallest possible number of black segments on the perimeter of the $5 \times 5$ square?
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The single square tile in the attached figure is divided by several diagonals into triangular regions; the triangular region corresponding to the bottom side is white, and the other regions touching the top side, left side, and right side are dark/black. Therefore, from the perspective of boundary colors, this kind of tile has exactly 1 white side and 3 black sides; rotating the tile is equivalent to choosing which direction this 1 white side faces.

Reasoning: Represent each tile placed in the 5×5 grid by “the direction faced by its unique white side.” The common side of two adjacent tiles must have the same color, so there are only two legal cases: both tiles face their white sides toward this common side, and the common side is white; or neither tile faces toward this common side, and the common side is black.

Let p be the number of white unit sides on the outer perimeter, and q be the number of internal white common sides. Each tile contributes exactly 1 white side, for a total of 25 white-side contributions. A white side on the outer perimeter consumes the white side of 1 tile, and an internal white common side is contributed by 1 white side from each of two adjacent tiles, so p + 2q = 25.

To make the number of black sides on the outer perimeter as small as possible, the number p of white sides on the outer perimeter must be made as large as possible, that is, q must be made as small as possible. A 5×5 grid has 3×3=9 internal cells; these internal tiles have no side on the outer perimeter of the large square, so their white sides must point toward adjacent tiles, and must be paired and matched into internal white common sides. Since 9 is odd, the 9 internal tiles cannot be completely paired only among themselves internally; at least 1 boundary tile is also needed to form a pair with some internal tile. Therefore, at least 10 tiles have their white sides used for internal pairing, that is, q ≥ 5.

From p + 2q = 25, we get p ≤ 25 - 10 = 15. The outer perimeter of the large square has 20 unit sides in total, so the number of black sides on the outer perimeter is at least 20 - 15 = 5.

This lower bound can be attained: mark the 5×5 grid with row and column coordinates, and let the internal white pairings be (1,2)-(2,2), (2,3)-(2,4), (3,2)-(4,2), (3,3)-(4,3), (3,4)-(4,4). These 5 pairs cover the 9 internal cells and 1 boundary cell. The remaining 15 boundary tiles all have their white sides placed facing outward. In this way, the outer perimeter has 15 white unit sides, so the black unit sides are 20 - 15 = 5.
